cases.sentence: Вдруг раздался ___, ни на что не похожий.
cases.translation: Suddenly a scream rang out, unlike anything else.
cases.explain: Крик is the subject of раздался (rang out), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Ужасный крик не умолкал, он сделался еще ужаснее, и, как бы дойдя до последнего предела ___, вдруг затих.
cases.translation: The terrible scream did not stop; it grew even more terrible, and, as if reaching the utmost limit of horror, suddenly fell silent.
cases.explain: The preposition до (up to) governs the genitive case, giving ужаса.

cases.sentence: Он припал головой к ___ кровати, чувствуя, что сердце его разрывается.
cases.translation: He pressed his head against the wood of the bed, feeling his heart being torn apart.
cases.explain: The preposition к (against/toward) governs the dative case, giving дереву.

cases.sentence: «Боже мой!» — сказал он, хватая за руку вошедшего ___.
cases.translation: "My God!" he said, grabbing the arm of the doctor who had just come in.
cases.explain: Доктора is the direct object of the transitive gerund хватая (grabbing); it is animate, so its accusative form matches the genitive: доктора.

cases.sentence: Рыдания и слезы радости, которых он никак не предвидел, с такой ___ поднялись в нем, что долго мешали ему говорить.
cases.translation: Sobs and tears of joy, which he had not at all foreseen, rose up in him with such force that they kept him from speaking for a long time.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case, giving силой.

cases.sentence: На том ___, где оно было прежде, было что-то страшное, и по виду напряжения, и по звуку, выходившему оттуда.
cases.translation: In the place where it had been before, there was something terrible, both in appearance and in the sound coming from there.
cases.explain: The preposition на (in/at) governs the prepositional case, giving месте.

reading.question: What time of night was it as this chapter begins?
options: The candles were all burning low
reading.correct: The candles were all burning low
reading.explain: The text says the candles were all burning down.

reading.ru: Был период отдыха, и он забылся.
reading.question: What was Levin doing during this period of relative calm?
options: He drifted off / lost himself for a moment
reading.correct: He drifted off / lost himself for a moment
reading.explain: There was a period of rest, and he lost himself in it for a moment.

reading.ru: Доктор склонил голову на бок, прислушиваясь, и одобрительно улыбнулся.
reading.question: How did the doctor react to the sudden terrible cry?
options: He tilted his head to listen and smiled approvingly
He panicked and ran to the bedroom
He told Levin to leave the house
reading.correct: He tilted his head to listen and smiled approvingly
reading.explain: The doctor inclined his head, listening, and smiled approvingly.

reading.ru: Лицо Лизаветы Петровны было строго и бледно, и все так же решительно, хотя челюсти ее немного подрагивали, и глаза ее были пристально устремлены на Китти.
reading.question: How is Lizaveta Petrovna's face described at this critical moment?
options: Stern and pale, though her jaw trembled slightly
reading.correct: Stern and pale, though her jaw trembled slightly
reading.explain: Lizaveta Petrovna's face was stern and pale, and though resolute, her jaw trembled slightly.

reading.ru: Левин схватился за голову и выбежал из комнаты.
reading.question: What did Levin do after Kitty cried out that it was terrible?
options: He clutched his head and ran out of the room
He tried to comfort her immediately
reading.correct: He clutched his head and ran out of the room
reading.explain: Levin clutched his head and ran out of the room.

reading.ru: Он даже не желал теперь ее жизни, он желал только прекращения этих ужасных страданий.
reading.question: What did Levin no longer want at this point in the ordeal?
options: He no longer wanted the child; he wanted only the terrible suffering to end
He no longer wanted the doctor present
He no longer wanted Lizaveta Petrovna in the room
He no longer cared about Kitty
reading.correct: He no longer wanted the child; he wanted only the terrible suffering to end
reading.explain: He no longer desired the child at all — he now hated it — and wished only for the end of the terrible suffering.

reading.ru: Не помня себя, он вбежал в спальню.
reading.question: What did Levin do on hearing the word "kончается" from the doctor?
options: Not remembering himself, he ran into the bedroom
He asked the doctor to repeat himself
reading.correct: Not remembering himself, he ran into the bedroom
reading.explain: Without remembering himself, he ran into the bedroom.

reading.ru: Он припал головой к дереву кровати, чувствуя, что сердце его разрывается.
reading.question: What did Levin do at the bed as the terrible cry continued?
options: He pressed his head against the wood of the bed, feeling his heart tearing apart
He called out for his mother-in-law
He prayed silently by the window
reading.correct: He pressed his head against the wood of the bed, feeling his heart tearing apart
reading.explain: He pressed his head to the wood of the bed, feeling his heart being torn apart.

reading.question: What happened to Levin emotionally once the crisis passed?
options: The taut strings within him all snapped, and sobs of joy overcame him
He became angry at the doctor
reading.correct: The taut strings within him all snapped, and sobs of joy overcame him
reading.explain: The text says the taut strings all gave way, and sobs and tears of joy he had not foreseen rose up in him.

reading.ru: Не беспокойтесь!» — услыхал Левин голос Лизаветы Петровны, шлепавший дрожавшую рукой спину ребенка.
reading.question: What did Levin hear Lizaveta Petrovna announce about the baby?
options: That the baby was alive, and it was a boy
That the baby was a girl
That the baby needed to see another doctor
reading.correct: That the baby was alive, and it was a boy
reading.explain: He heard Lizaveta Petrovna's voice saying, "Alive! Alive! And a boy too!"

reading.ru: Китти была жива, страдания кончились, и он был невыразимо счастлив.
reading.question: How did Levin feel once he understood Kitty was alive and well?
reading.explain: The text says Kitty was alive, the suffering was over, and he was inexpressibly happy.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows that Levin remains calm despite hearing a terrifying scream?
sentences: Вдруг раздался крик, ни на что не похожий.
Крик был так страшен, что Левин даже не вскочил, но, не переводя дыхания, испуганно-вопросительно посмотрел на доктора.
Доктор склонил голову набок, прислушиваясь, и одобрительно улыбнулся.
Все было так необыкновенно, что уж ничто не поражало Левина.
«Верно, так надо», – подумал он и продолжал сидеть.
highlight.explain: Although the scream is dreadful, Levin stays composed and looks at the doctor for reassurance, who nods approvingly.

highlight.question: Which sentences express Levin's darkest thoughts about what is happening?
sentences: Но, что б они ни говорили, он знал, что теперь все погибло.
Прислонившись головой к притолоке, он стоял в соседней комнате и слышал чей-то никогда не слыханный им визг, рев, и он знал, что это кричало то, что было прежде Кити.
Уже ребенка он давно не желал.
Он даже не желал теперь ее жизни, он желал только прекращения этих ужасных страданий.
highlight.explain: Levin believes everything is lost, hates the child, and now wishes only for an end to Kitty's terrible suffering.

highlight.question: Which sentence best captures the horror of what Levin sees when he looks at Kitty?
sentences: Первое, что он увидал, это было лицо Лизаветы Петровны.
Оно было еще нахмуренное и строже.
На том месте, где оно было прежде, было что-то страшное и по виду напряжения и по звуку, выходившему оттуда.
Он припал головой к дереву кровати, чувствуя, что сердце его разрывается.
highlight.explain: Instead of her face, something terrible and strained appears, expressing the immense physical anguish she is enduring.

highlight.question: Which sentence(s) describe Levin's sudden transition from despair to joy?
sentences: И вдруг из того таинственного и ужасного, нездешнего мира, в котором он жил эти двадцать два часа, Левин мгновенно почувствовал себя перенесенным в прежний, обычный мир, но сияющий теперь таким новым светом счастья, что он не перенес его.
Рыдания и слезы радости, которых он никак не предвидел, с такою силой поднялись в нем, колебля все его тело, что долго мешали ему говорить.
highlight.explain: In an instant, Levin feels transported from the mysterious, terrifying world into the ordinary world now radiant with happiness.
